title: Cluster Lifeguard Panel - compact health & throughput controls
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design an ultra-compact control panel for Dedicated capacity clusters that surfaces GPU pool health, recent throughput, and quick autoscaling/burst controls. The panel (Cluster Lifeguard) is intended for on-call and SRE workflows: low visual noise, fast triage actions, and safe policy edits. This ticket covers initial flows, mid-fidelity prototypes, developer handoff notes, and a short round of user validation with platform SREs.
design_notes: Goals: (1) enable 10s triage time to actionable decision, (2) let admins apply temporary burst or throttles within a strict policy guardrail, (3) show clear cost signal inline so ops can weigh trade-offs. Key patterns explored: micro-sparkline + health pill, hysteresis slider (min/target/max), 'safe presets' menu with immutable rollback, and an inline 'what changed' timeline.
decisions: Prefer single-row compact presentation with expandable detail drawer rather than multi-column card to keep dashboard density high.
Expose three quick actions: Apply Burst (timeboxed), Set Target Throughput, and Revert to Policy. Each action requires a confirmation modal with estimated cost delta.
Autoscale presets will be curated by platform team and surfaced as immutable entries; custom presets allowed but must pass a dry-run validation in staging.
Telemetry will show 60s and 5m sparkline overlays to avoid alarm noise from transient spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Figma mid-fi prototype for compact panel with expanded detail drawer produced and shared: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/cluster-lifeguard-v1
Front-end prototype (React story) demonstrating: sparkline, health pill, hysteresis slider, preset menu, and confirmation modal

Design specification doc in Confluence with interaction states, accessibility contrast numbers, keyboard shortcuts, and copy for confirmation flows: https://confluence.company/rd/cluster-lifeguard-spec
Two 30-minute usability sessions with SRE and Platform PMs completed and notes attached to ticket
Integration hooks defined for telemetry API (metrics keys) and cost estimator endpoint; engineering agrees on API surface in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234

comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava Chen: Initial sketches uploaded to Figma. Chose three density candidates: minimalist, compact, compact+detail. Invited SREs for quick review.

2026-02-18 - Marcus Rivera: Engineering assessment: hysteresis slider requires backend enforcement to avoid oscillation; will add sticky debounce and server-side min-interval of 5m for target changes.

2026-02-25 - Priya Kapoor (Platform PM): Request to include explicit cost delta callout in confirmation modal. Suggested showing estimated token-cost per-minute and projected 1h cost for burst durations.
2026-03-03 - Design review: Team prefers compact variant with drawer. Agreed to cap burst duration options to 10m/30m/1h presets to reduce accidental long-running bursts.
2026-03-09 - Marcus Rivera: Front-end story implemented; linking PR for telemetry hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/558
2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Usability session notes attached to Drive. SREs liked the revert-to-policy flow but asked for clearer state when a rollback is pending. Added to tasks.
review_feedback: Design Ops: Request to document token-class color semantics used in health pill so other dashboards are consistent.
Security: Add a note - changes to autoscale or burst must be logged to audit trail and require 2FA for org owners. Marked security_review_required.
PM: Ensure cost estimator uses committed capacity pricing tiers for Dedicated customers; display both 'incremental cost' and 'marginal per-token' estimates.
Frontend: Suggest limiting animation in the sparkline to 'on-hover' to reduce CPU usage on pages with many panels.
